rationale: MacBook power users do pay for indie utilities (Amphetamine, CleanMyMac, etc.), giving some willingness-to-pay signal (score 5), but the buyer is a broad consumer rather than a named B2B/prosumer with a budget line (buyer clarity 5). More critically, building a reliable macOS system-level tool that reads power and sleep event history requires native macOS APIs and a distributable app — not something buildable via Claude + a web form + Stripe. Total of 4.7 falls below the validate threshold of 5.5.
solution_plan: Not viable for this factory. A macOS menu-bar diagnostic app requires native macOS development (Swift/Objective-C or an Electron wrapper with OS-level API access), App Store distribution or notarization, and OS-version compatibility maintenance. None of that is buildable with Claude + a landing page + Stripe in a week by a non-technical solo operator. This is a valid indie-developer opportunity but requires a developer co-founder or pre-built macOS app expertise.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai_min (4 < 6) and operational_autonomy_min (5 < 7) build gates. Total (4.7) also below validate threshold — drop.
